title: How a Zipper Actually Works
text: This sound is one of the oldest tricks in your closet. Zoom in, and every tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath. Push two rows together by hand, and they just slide apart. The angle is wrong. The secret is inside the slider. A Y-shaped channel. Pull up, and it squeezes both rows into one, tilting each tooth until its bump drops into the next one's hollow. Pull down, and the same Y pries them apart. Now check your own zipper. There's a good chance it says YKK. One Japanese company makes a huge share of the world's zippers. And the name? A rubber boot company, in 1923, named it after the sound. Zip.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipper (tooth projection and recess; Y-shaped slider channel; B. F. Goodrich named it 'zipper' on rubber galoshes in 1923)
